title: Mentioning specific marital status or lack of dependents may predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning the education of children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who describe the microfinance program's role in providing loans without collateral may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention contributing to community economic growth or food production may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention their past loan repayment history fund faster.
Pitches that explicitly mention age, marital status, number of children, or educational status are associated with slower funding speeds for both men and women.
Male borrowers who mention the specific number of previous loan applications may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include specific details about their daily routine or travel distances may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention their specific town or region may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers in the education sector who specify that the loan supports both business and schooling may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list a wide variety of specific inventory items fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayments predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who explicitly name their institutional partner fund faster.
